hypotheses.subject: io-shop process heap (memory_used_bytes / heap MiB of 2048MiB limit)
hypotheses.summary: A memory leak in the long-running io-shop process: from 2026-09-19T23:50Z heap climbs monotonically from ~460MB baseline to 1.39GB of the 2GB limit with constant request volume (1200/min) and no process restart (process_start_time_seconds unchanged at 1789841975.987538), with GC/allocation pressure dragging p50 from ~45ms to 173ms and p95 from ~215ms to 729ms after 00:09. No deploy or config change is recorded in any window read.

supporting_evidence.claim: memory_used_bytes rises steadily without release: 449133438 at 23:42 -> 596517327 at 23:54 -> 966146095 at 00:06 -> 1394557854 at 00:19, against a flat memory_limit_bytes of 2147483648
process_start_time_seconds constant at 1789841975.987538 across every bucket - the process never restarted, so the growth accumulates in one process
WARN io-shop: heap at 1052MiB of 2048MiB limit ... 1322MiB of 2048MiB limit (monotonic +30MiB per minute)
request_volume flat at 1200 per minute throughout, so memory growth is not load-driven
p50_ms 43 at 00:00 rising to 173 at 00:19 and p95_ms 209 -> 729, degradation tracking heap growth
Every recorded change to io-shop from 2026-09-12T00:00:00Z to 2026-09-19T23:54:00Z. (nothing changed in this window)
Every recorded change to io-shop from 2026-09-19T23:00:00Z to 2026-09-20T00:19:35Z. (nothing changed in this window)

hypotheses.summary: An unrecorded change (deploy or flag flip) at ~23:49-23:50 introduced the leaking code path; the change channel simply has no entry for it. The evidence shows the leak but nothing naming a change, so this remains speculative.

supporting_evidence.claim: memory_used_bytes breaks from the 449-480MB band exactly at 2026-09-19T23:50:00Z (480106284) and never returns
change log returned '(nothing changed in this window)' for both the 7-day lookback and the incident window, so no deploy or toggle can be named

hypotheses.summary: The persistent 'UpstreamTimeout: payment authorization timed out' errors on the account page could indicate an upstream payment dependency slowing/hanging, with in-flight requests or retry buffers piling up in memory. However these errors run at the same 1-2 per minute rate for the whole hour before onset, so they look like steady background noise rather than the trigger.

supporting_evidence.claim: ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - UpstreamTimeout: payment authorization timed out
Same 1-2 UpstreamTimeout lines per minute at 23:00, before memory departs baseline at 23:50, and unchanged afterwards - no step change in the error channel
